chunks: Why PCB rework is needed. The question: Why may rework be needed?
Boards need rework for four reasons. Something went wrong when the board was built (a defect). The design itself had a mistake. A part was bad.
Or someone deliberately changed the design after boards were made. Knowing which one applies tells you what to fix, so the problem does not return.
Think of a long printed book. Even if the printer makes only one typo per 20,000 words, a whole book still ends up with a few.
A board is like that: each solder joint is one tiny chance to fail, and a board has hundreds or thousands of them.
The four causes match too: a printing slip (assembly defect), an author's mistake (design error), a bad batch of paper (component problem), and a revised edition (planned change).
Each cause points at a different part of the process. Treat the leaves as the fix; the rework itself is just a symptom.
Solder joint: one soldered connection between a part and the board. Defect: a joint or part that is not made correctly, such as two pins bridged by solder.
First-pass yield: the share of boards that work the first time with no rework. Root cause: the real reason a fault happens, as opposed to the symptom you repaired.
ECO (engineering change order): a formal design change made after boards exist. ppm: parts per million, so 50 ppm is 50 in every million.
Say a board has 1000 joints, and each has a 50 ppm chance of being bad. That is a chance of 0. 00005 per joint. Over the whole board, you expect 1000 times 0. 00005 = 0.
05 defects. About 95 boards in 100 come out clean, and about 5 in 100 need rework. Now suppose most of that rework is the same pad on the same part every time.
The fix is to correct that pad design, not to keep reworking. That is the whole idea.

"Rework is needed for four reasons: manufacturing defects like bridges, opens or tombstones, design errors like a wrong footprint or missing pull-up, component failures from ESD or bad lots, and changes like ECOs or obsolescence.
Even a tiny per-joint defect rate adds up: 1000 joints at 50 ppm gives about 5% of boards needing rework.
I try to find the root cause so we fix the process or the design, not just the board."
Quick check. A footprint error causes the same part to fail on every prototype board. Which category is this?
